item.title: Metrics
item.description:
Metrics provide valuable insights into how users engage with the designs, allowing us to understand usage patterns, identify trends, and make data-driven decisions to improve the user experience.

The design catalog can be accessed from the Layer5 Cloud catalog page at Layer5 Cloud Catalog.

Design Capabilities

Designs can be imported, exported, versioned, forked, merged, snapshotted, published, shared, embedded, templatized, and more. Learn more about Designs

item.description:

item.title: Exploring the Catalog
item.description:
The Cloud Catalog is the central hub for well-architected cloud and cloud native patterns and best practices templates. Here, you can discover and share designs with the wider community.

Viewing Catalog Items 🔗

Meshery Catalog displays all published designs in an organized, searchable format.

Top Performers 🔗

At the top of the page, you can find the Top Performers section. This provides a snapshot of the Leaderboard, highlighting the most popular designs based on various metrics.

item.title: Catalog
item.description:
Public Catalog: https://cloud.layer5.io/catalog

The Cloud Catalog is a web-based, public catalog to facilitate easy discovery of existing designs. Designs that are published into the catalog can be, but are not always curated for known best practices and patterns. Content is published at cloud.layer5.io/catalog, and one-click import of catalog content into Meshery Server is seamlessly integrated.

Content Visibility 🔗

Each item in the catalog comes with an associated level of visibility.

item.title: Build a GCP Data Pipeline Design
item.description: In this tutorial you follow Zara Osei, Team Admin of the Orbital Labs Infrastructure Team, as she models the team’s Google Cloud data pipeline in Kanvas. The pipeline ingests events through Pub/Sub, processes them with Dataflow, writes analytical results to BigQuery, archives raw payloads to Cloud Storage, and runs alongside a GKE cluster. The result is a design named data-pipeline-gcp: a reviewable, shareable model of the architecture that lives in the team’s workspace instead of in a slide deck.

item.title: Designer
item.description:
Designer mode is where you author a Kanvas design. You compose infrastructure from versioned components, configure each one against its schema, connect components with relationships, annotate the result, and validate or deploy it, all on one canvas that every collaborator edits at the same time. Designer works on intent: what you want to run. Operator works on live state: what is running.

A design is a shared document 🔗

Everything on the canvas is an entry in one design document: every component you configure, every relationship, and every annotation you draw. The canvas draws that document. Moving a node, applying a layout, or hiding a layer writes into the design. As a result:

item.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
item.description:
Kanvas binds every shortcut to both modifier keys. On Windows and Linux use Ctrl. On macOS use Cmd. The tables write the modifier as Ctrl/Cmd.

Kanvas ignores shortcuts while you type in a text field, so typing a label, a comment or a search never triggers one. Open the same list inside the app with Ctrl/Cmd + /.

Modes and navigation 🔗

Shortcut Action Designer Operator
V or Esc Switch to the Select tool. Esc also closes open menus and dialogs. Yes Yes
H Switch to the Pan tool. Yes Yes
Space (hold) Pan while the key is down, then return to the Select tool. Yes Yes
Ctrl/Cmd + P Turn the Pencil tool on or off. Yes No
Ctrl/Cmd + E Turn the Pen tool on or off. Yes No
Ctrl/Cmd + + Zoom in. Yes Yes
Ctrl/Cmd + - Zoom out. Yes Yes
\ (backslash) Open the Layers panel. Yes Yes
Ctrl/Cmd + / Open the shortcut reference in the help drawer. Yes Yes
Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + / Open the Help Center. Yes Yes

The tools are described in Tool Modes.

item.title: Kanvas Designer Overview
Pinning Models to Dock
item.description:
Transcript:

Five has found that he frequently references the same set of models while designing. If you know that you’ll be using components from a model frequently, you can pin that model for easy retrieval of its components. To pin a model to the dock in Layer5 Kanvas, click the pin icon next to the model. The model will now be accessible in the dock for quick use.
